clue.text: Victor Hugo's debut covered by poet

indicators.note: being covered by the poet's name means the letter goes inside that name

parts.note: Thomas Campion was an Elizabethan poet and composer

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the opening letter of Hugo's

explanation.surface: The French novelist's first work is overshadowed by a rival poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor Hugo' reads as one name, but Victor is the definition and Hugo only supplies its initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor wins, and a champion is the winner of a contest.

clue.text: Caption: "Man had concealed a note"

indicators.note: the letters of the man's words hide the next letter inside them

parts.note: he'd is short for he had
a line is a short note, as in drop me a line

explanation.surface: A newspaper caption announces that a man kept a message secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' puts A inside the contraction for 'man had'; a line is a short written note, as in 'drop me a line'.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title in large type above a newspaper story, a kind of caption.

clue.text: To tighten one's belt, bring the tips together

definitions.meaning: to economise and live within one's means
literally, join the two extremities so they touch

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to manage on a small income; literally it describes the ends of something touching.

clue.text: At regular intervals dimwit sat for a copyist

indicators.note: every third letter of the words dimwit sat for a is taken away, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A dull-witted person keeps posing for an artist who copies.
explanation.walkthrough: Of DIMWITSATFORA, drop the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th and 13th letters (D, W, S, F, A), and the remaining letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copyist imitates the work of others.

clue.text: Twelve changes do annoy

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes into a new order

explanation.surface: Changes are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges DO ANNOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Noonday is midday, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: During trial, ask about the state of the North-West

indicators.note: the answer runs during the words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: In a court case, someone questions the condition of the north-western region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a reversal sign, but it only supplies the final A of the run in triAL ASK About.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the US state in the far north-west of North America.

clue.text: Take a trip to an ancient city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone travels to visit a ruined old town.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour is to travel round a place on a trip.

clue.text: Producing screams — a murder

indicators.note: producing here means bringing out the letters in another order

explanation.surface: A killing that sets people screaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Producing' rearranges SCREAMS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the brutal killing of many people, mass murder.

clue.text: Sooner state "It's a show"

definitions.meaning: the US state nicknamed after the 'Sooners', settlers who claimed land before the official start in 1889
the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical of 1943

explanation.definitionFit: The Sooner State is the official nickname of this US state, which also titles the famous Broadway musical.

clue.text: 24 oars in a galley

definitions.meaning: the answer to 24 down, TILT; an aircraft tilting to turn is said to do this
a row of oars set side by side in an ancient galley is called by this word

explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to the answer of 24 down, TILT, which is one definition by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft tilts when it banks into a turn, and a tier of oars in a galley is a bank.

clue.text: See town road's snarled up, and back down

indicators.note: traffic that is snarled up is jumbled and tangled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist is told to look at the town road jammed with traffic and to reverse out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled up' rearranges the letters of SEE TOWN ROADS; the apostrophe adds no letter. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement humbly, admitting error, is to back down.

clue.text: The ceiling is all Greek, it seems to me

definitions.meaning: the ceiling is literally above you

definitions.text: is all Greek, it seems to me

explanation.definitionFit: The ceiling is literally above you; figuratively, something too hard to grasp is beyond your understanding.

clue.text: Ring a small group of soldiers round

indicators.note: turning round means the whole string of letters is read the other way

parts.note: ten is a small group, as of people
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A call goes out to gather a handful of troops together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the whole run TENGIS backwards. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a seal set in a finger ring, often called a signet ring.

clue.text: Lecturer given two bills, the second cut by a half

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: the second of the two bills is split open and the half goes into it

parts.note: another account, again abbreviated AC
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A university teacher receives two invoices, the later one halved.
explanation.walkthrough: Both bills are AC (account); the second is cut open by DEMI, giving A(DEMI)C. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a university teacher or scholar, such as a lecturer.

clue.text: It's a waste, eating just a soupcon of suet pudding

indicators.note: the waste swallows the letter, putting it inside

parts.note: a desert is a barren waste

indicators.note: a soupcon is a tiny taste, so only the first letter of suet is used

explanation.surface: Someone complains that eating even a little suet pudding is a wasted effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts S (the first letter of suet) inside DESERT. 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudding in British usage is the sweet course, also called afters.

clue.text: Gone — pound that's spent

parts.note: gone means dead
to pound is to beat

explanation.surface: Something finished is worn out after all its pounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-beat is an informal word for exhausted, wholly spent.

clue.text: Bunk low in a vessel

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a vase is a vessel
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A cow bellowing inside a bottle, or a sailor's sleeping berth.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunk is a verb here: to do a bunk is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: To bunk, or do a bunk, is to run away, as is to vamoose.

clue.text: A tin in this way used as a capital ornament

parts.note: a can is a tin
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A piece of tin is used in this fashion to decorate the top of a column.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'capital' is the head of a column, not a city; 'used as a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus leaves are the carved decoration on Corinthian column heads.

clue.text: You may see the answer, but not Louis, unfortunately

indicators.note: things turned out badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone finds the answer, but it is not Louis, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like a deletion sign, but it is part of the fodder: 'unfortunately' rearranges NOT LOUIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is the answer to a problem or puzzle.

clue.text: Ice becoming finally more full of holes

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of becoming

parts.note: lacier, like lace, means having more holes

explanation.surface: Ice that grows ever more porous.
explanation.walkthrough: G, the final letter of 'becoming', then LACIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacier is a slow river of ice.

clue.text: Bringing up the rear, in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming behind every other one, last of the lot
nevertheless, when all is said and done

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, behind everyone means last in line; as an idiom it means nevertheless.

clue.text: Granted, it's a nasty trait

parts.note: greed is an unpleasant trait of character

explanation.surface: Admitted: it's a bad trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed, as an assent, means conceded or allowed, as granted does.

clue.text: A mineral found all round the East — it's ancient

indicators.note: the gold surrounds the letter, placed inside it

parts.note: gold is a precious material mined from the earth
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Precious ore discovered across the Orient is very old.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then GOLD with E inside. 'it's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has lasted for a very long time, as anything ancient has.

clue.text: Sweet and black, say, a drink

annotationWithheld.why: Sweet and black, say, a drink: SCOTCH is the drink, but no sound reading gives BUTTER from 'and black, say'; the scan confirms the wording and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Sweet and black, say, a drink

clue.text: Incline to enter the lists

definitions.meaning: to joust in a medieval tournament arena

explanation.definitionFit: To tilt is to slope or lean; it also means to charge with a lance, as knights did in the lists.

clue.text: Arrange overtime

indicators.note: turned over means the word is read the other way

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Someone sets up extra hours at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtime' looks like one word, but 'over' turns TIDE (time) backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to put material in order for publication, to arrange it.

clue.text: The lot look round -gosh, that's nonsense

indicators.note: the two words go around the exclamation, which sits between them

parts.note: all means the lot
to eye is to look at
my! is an exclamation like gosh!

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the whole lot and exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts MY inside the outer pair. 'All my eye' is a dated British expression for rubbish; 'my!' is an old exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: All my eye, or all my eye and Betty Martin, is an old British expression for rubbish.

clue.text: One who dwells in desert nomadically

indicators.note: nomads wander, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Describes a Bedouin, living in the desert as a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nomadically' rearranges IN DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident lives in a place, as anyone who dwells there does.
